Outlet: AFP via Yahoo Finance UK, Fri 6 November 2026 at 9:47 pm GMT
Tech stocks stage partial rebound while dollar gains after US jobs data

Tech shares recovered Friday after Thursday's collapse, with the Nasdaq climbing 1.1 percent following stronger-than-expected US employment data that boosted the dollar. The US economy added 165,000 jobs last month, significantly exceeding analyst predictions. The unemployment rate dipped to 4.1 percent.

The Nasdaq entered correction territory after dropping over 10 percent in the past month, driven by concerns that Democratic election victories could obstruct AI data center expansion plans.

Texas Governor-elect Gina Hinojosa: "We have always been a pro-business state in Texas, but what changes now with me as governor is it has to be a partnership that benefits Texans."
Jose Torres of Interactive Brokers: "Markets could receive an additional boost if the Democrats soften their tone on AI."

Asian markets suffered significantly Thursday, with Tokyo and Seoul closing down 6 percent each. Samsung fell 6.4 percent, while SK hynix dropped 10 percent on Seoul's Kospi index.

Key market closes (around 2120 GMT):
New York Dow: DOWN 0.5% at 51,285.73
S&P 500: UP 0.3% at 7,376.86
Nasdaq: UP 1.1% at 24,579.42
FTSE 100: DOWN 1.0% at 10,673.94
Euro/dollar: DOWN to $1.1138 from $1.1219
